subtopics.title: Cost Price, Selling Price and Percentage Profit

questions.question: Ingredients of R95, R120, R185 and R60 for a batch of 100 vetkoek give a cost price per vetkoek of:
Selling at R8 with a cost price of R4,60, the percentage profit on cost is:
The selling price is best described as:
options: A number fixed by the ingredients
A decision informed by cost price, competitors' prices and what customers will bear

questions.question: Takings of R7 120 this year against R6 400 last year is an increase of:

subtopics.title: Break-even: Where Loss Turns into Profit

questions.question: The R300 pitch fee is a fixed cost because:
options: It is spent before the first customer and does not change with the number sold
It increases with every vetkoek made

questions.question: Each vetkoek sold at R8 with variable cost R4,60 contributes toward the fixed cost:
The break-even number of vetkoek is 300 ÷ 3,40 = 88,2, reported as:
options: 89 — at 88 the stall is still R0,80 short, at 89 it is R2,60 ahead

questions.question: On the break-even graph, the loss at a quantity left of the crossing appears as:
options: The slope of the income line
The point where the cost line starts
The horizontal distance between the lines
The vertical gap where the cost line rides above the income line

subtopics.title: Interest and Banking, Year by Year

questions.question: R6 000 in a fixed deposit at 7% compound grows in year one to:
Year two's interest is R449,40, larger than year one's R420, because:
options: The 7% now works on the grown balance of R6 420 — interest earning interest

questions.question: After three years, compound at 7% gives R7 350,26 against simple interest's R7 260 — a difference of:
A credit card differs from a debit card because credit:
options: Spends the bank's money, which must be repaid — with interest if late

subtopics.title: Inflation: When the Same Trolley Costs More

questions.question: At 6% inflation, an ingredient basket of R1 850 costs next year:
Bread rising from R15,50 to R17,05 is an inflation rate of:
options: 10% — the increase of 1,55 divided by the OLD price of 15,50

questions.question: Two years of 6% inflation multiplies prices by:
options: 1,06 × 1,06 = 1,1236, because the second rise stands on the first

questions.question: Savings earning nothing while inflation runs at 6%:
options: Are unaffected, since the rand amount is unchanged
Lose about 6% of their buying power each year

questions.question: The cost price of R4,60 is called the floor because:
options: Selling below it makes every sale dig the hole deeper
It is the lowest price competitors charge
Prices cannot legally go below it

questions.question: Measured against cost, the R3,40 profit is 73,9%; measured against the selling price it would be 42,5%. The paper expects:
options: Profit on COST, with the base written next to the answer

questions.question: The budget projected R500 for ingredients and the till says R460. The one-sentence analysis is:
options: The projection was wrong so the budget fails
R40 under budget, because oil was on special

subtopics.title: How Many Before We Stop Losing

questions.question: At dawn, before any sales, the stall is already R300 down because:
options: The pitch fee is paid whether the day goes well or badly

questions.question: The 89th vetkoek is special because:
options: It tips the stall from loss into profit — before it sales reduce the loss, after it each sale is full profit
It is the last of the batch

questions.question: In the race picture of the graph, income catches cost because:
options: Income climbs R8 a step against cost's R4,60, despite cost's R300 head start

questions.question: Raising the price from R8 to R9 moves break-even from 89 to:
options: 69 — each sale now pushes R4,40 against the R300

subtopics.title: The Bank's Staircase and the Trolley That Grows

questions.question: The bank staircase's steps get taller each year because:
options: Interest starts earning its own interest
The bank raises the rate annually

questions.question: The staircase's dark twin is:
options: A debt at compound interest climbing the same steps when nothing is repaid

questions.question: Finding an inflation rate from two prices always divides by:
options: The OLD price — bread from R15,50 to R17,05 is 1,55 over 15,50, ten percent

questions.question: Money earning 7% while prices climb 6% is truly growing by:
options: Only the sliver between the two rates
